_comment: MOCKED transcript for CHEM 201, shaped like Bee's new-utterance stream events. Timestamps are ms offsets from session start, applied at load time. Speakers are role labels only, never identity (no voice ID on Bee/Alexa+). The `label` field is a hand-written ground truth used only to score the two classifiers against each other in the demo; nothing in the pipeline reads it.

utterances.speaker: instructor
utterances.text: Okay everyone, today we will cover reaction kinetics and then start on equilibrium.
utterances.label: none
utterances.note: Says what the class is about. On the syllabus. A student writes this themselves.

utterances.speaker: instructor
utterances.text: The rate constant depends on temperature according to the Arrhenius equation, which relates k to the activation energy.
utterances.label: none

utterances.speaker: instructor
utterances.text: That assignment I mentioned has not moved, it is still where the syllabus says.
utterances.label: none
utterances.note: Hard negative, verified: the rules classifier calls this a deadline_change because 'assignment' and 'moved' sit inside its window. Nothing changed, so it is not an announcement.

utterances.speaker: student_a
utterances.text: Wait, is the exam next Thursday or the Thursday after?

utterances.speaker: instructor
utterances.text: Good question, so the answer to that one is it's the Thursday after, the 14th, not next week.
utterances.label: relayed_answer

utterances.speaker: instructor
utterances.text: Something I should have said at the start: I am not holding office hours on Thursday, come Wednesday instead.
utterances.label: contact_instruction
utterances.note: Hard positive. No keyword the rules look for. Purely procedural, and nowhere in anyone's notes.

utterances.speaker: instructor
utterances.text: Quick heads up, the problem set essay is now due Monday, not Friday, since the printer in the lab is down.
utterances.label: deadline_change

utterances.speaker: instructor
utterances.text: To answer this question properly you need to integrate the rate law first.
utterances.label: none
utterances.note: Hard negative, verified: the rules classifier calls this a relayed_answer on the phrase 'to answer ... question'. It is course content.

utterances.speaker: instructor
utterances.text: This will be on the exam, so make sure you understand the difference between zero order and first order kinetics.
utterances.label: exam_signal

utterances.speaker: instructor
utterances.text: Forget what the syllabus says about the second midterm being closed book, it is open book now.
utterances.label: exam_signal
utterances.note: Hard positive. Contradicts a written document, which is exactly the case where a student's own notes will be wrong.

utterances.speaker: instructor
utterances.text: Integrating the rate law over time gives us the concentration as a function of time for a first order reaction.
utterances.label: none

utterances.speaker: instructor
utterances.text: Any questions on that? No? Good, let's keep going.
utterances.label: none
utterances.note: Managing the room. No information at all.

utterances.speaker: student_b
utterances.text: did you get the notes from last class, mine are a mess
utterances.note: Side conversation between two students, neither an expected speaker. Dropped by rule 3 before any classifier sees it.

utterances.speaker: student_c
utterances.text: no i missed it, was there anything important

utterances.speaker: instructor
utterances.text: The lab report template on the site is the old one, I will replace it tonight, so do not start from it yet.
utterances.label: contact_instruction
utterances.note: Hard positive. Nobody writes this down because it sounds like housekeeping until it costs you a week.

utterances.speaker: instructor
utterances.text: One more thing before you go, we're moving to room 214 for the rest of the week because of a scheduling conflict here.
utterances.label: room_change

utterances.speaker: instructor
utterances.text: We are moving to room temperature for the next part of the demonstration, so the rate constant drops.
utterances.label: none
utterances.note: Hard negative, verified: the rules classifier calls this a room_change on 'moving ... room'. The class is not moving anywhere.

utterances.speaker: instructor
utterances.text: If you want feedback on your lab report before it's due, email me by Friday and I'll get to it over the weekend.
utterances.label: contact_instruction

utterances.speaker: instructor
utterances.text: Students email me by the dozen about this, and the answer is always in chapter four.
utterances.label: none
utterances.note: Hard negative, verified: the rules classifier calls this a contact_instruction on 'email ... me ... by'. It instructs nobody to do anything.

utterances.speaker: instructor
utterances.text: Alright, that's it for today, see you Wednesday.
utterances.label: none

utterances.speaker: instructor
utterances.text: This last comment is after the session officially ended and should be dropped by rule 1 regardless of its content, this will be on the exam too.
utterances.note: Outside the session window. Dropped by rule 1 before any classifier sees it.
